title: Weave a pastry strip into a pie lattice
instruction: Weave the loose pastry strip over one strip and under the other on the pie. Leave all three strips intact, flat across the crust, and release them.
context: Weaving a lattice crust requires lifting soft pastry, passing another strip underneath and replacing it without tearing or undoing the crossing.
setup: A loose aluminium tart pan, 180 mm inside diameter, 190 mm rim diameter and 36 mm deep, holds a bottom crust and level canned apple filling; prepared mass about 550 g. Three fresh shortcrust pastry strips are each 250 × 25 × 2 mm. Two lie north–south across the pie, 64 mm apart. The third lies east–west on a 180 × 180 × 42 mm wooden board to the left, 50 mm south of the pie centreline, with 35 mm overhang at each end. The board is level with the pie surface. Nothing is fixed or pre-woven. Pie centre: (350, 25) mm; board centre: (130, 25) mm on the YAM worktop. Both arms have washable stainless finger extensions with 40 × 6 × 1 mm working leaves. Use food-safe gripper/wrist sleeves and a washable catch mat in real trials. The README specifies dough preparation and reset.
scoring: Score after both grippers are open and at least 50 mm clear for 3 seconds. Award 0.5 if the cross-strip passes over one lengthwise strip and under the other, with both crossings within 80 mm of the pie centre. Either order is valid. Award 1.0 if all three strips also rest flat on the pie (portions over the filling no more than 12 mm above it) and reach the crust at both ends: each end reaches the 86 mm-radius inner crust and extends at least 60 mm to its side of the centre along its strip’s main direction (north–south or east–west). Otherwise score 0. A strip torn through, lost off the work area, or a pie tilted more than 30 degrees at any time gives zero. Judge crossing order, crust reach, flatness and release with photographs/video and a ruler. Trimming and straightness are not scored.
fidelity: Pastry uses passive chains of 24 contact-bearing sectors, with bending, twisting, native collisions and breakable joints. Finite native pinches move it; no scripted folds or body-position writes follow reset. Stretch, tackiness, plastic flow and temperature response are omitted; stiffness and force limits are uncalibrated. Pan, crust and filling are one rigid body. Real-trial sleeves and catch mat are not rendered. No physical preparation or material validation is claimed.
reset_notes: Use three fresh strips and a fresh level pie surface per attempt. Follow the README’s same-product dough, temperature and preparation intervals; discard cracked, dry or stuck strips. Wash contact extensions and replace protective sleeves. Restore the measured layout with no initial crossings.
